nodes.title: ⚙️ Settings:

en.text:
## ⚙️ Settings

**Load Image 🖼️**
- ***I cannot stress enough*** 🗑️ in, 🗑️ out.
- **Load a clean, high quality, front facing headshot.** This is image one.
- **Optional Image 2 🖼️** (image two) adds a second look at the character. I suggest a smiling one here and a serious one up top.

**Prompt Enhancer 📝 (Character Anchor)**
- It runs **once per list**, not once per prompt. It reads your **Character anchor ⚓** and both pictures and writes one short description of the character: face, eyes, hair, skin, build.
- It never describes clothing, pose, background or light. Every prompt in the list sets those itself.
- Preset **Character Anchor**, seed fixed, so the description stays the same run after run. Change the seed if you want it rewritten.
- The prompt lists are already written out the way Flux 3 Klein needs them: framing, camera height, exact pose and where the face points ("true 90-degree side profile facing the right edge of the frame, with only one eye visible"), outfit, background, light.
- Writing your own rows? Describe the camera, the pose and where the face points, not just "profile view".
- The **Final Prompt** box shows what Flux 3 Klein actually got.

**Ksampler Settings**
- **steps total**: 15. That's close to Black Forest Labs' setting for Flux 3 Klein (16). You can go as low as 4 for speed, it just loses some detail.
- **CFG (Classifier Free Guidance):** 1.0. The distilled model doesn't use CFG, so leave it alone.
- Speed Boost is off: it changes the framing on Flux 3 Klein edits.

**Prompt list Selector 📝✅**
- Choose from one of the lists or create your own
- creating a custom list
   - Enter your prompt, then separate them by hitting return.
   - Each new line is a prompt, so be careful


### Instructions:

- Load an upper torso headshot only
- Name your character
- Determine the size of the image output in the aspect ratio node
   - 💡 if you generate a lot in a certain size (for me it's 1080x1350), it is best to make a dataset matching that
- Review the prompts to make sure they match your character
- 👋 The *Generation anchor ⚓* names the pictures (image 1 = face, image 2 = body), tells Flux 3 Klein to keep the face, hair, skin and body and to ignore the clothing in them, plus a few quality modifiers. This is for *realism*.
- The *Character anchor ⚓* is a few notes about your character. The Prompt Enhancer turns them into the full description.
- enter the **anchor text⚓**:
   - examples: "fit, blonde hair, green eyes, medium breasts"

**LoRAs**
- Place realism LoRAs or style LoRAs here (made for Flux 3 Klein).
- ⚠️ I have no character LoRAs. I cannot tell you if this helps or not. Try it out and let me know

**💾 Save area**
- The Run # is added to the prefix so that you can tell the difference. Reset as necessary

**💡 Tips & Tricks**
- Use a **Headshot** as your main image.
- **🗑️ in = 🗑️ out.** If the quality of your image is low, then the results will match.
- ⚠️ Flux 3 Klein keeps what's in the picture unless the prompt changes it. The anchor already says to ignore the original clothing: *if you make custom prompts, describe the outfit you want.*
- Use the pre-scale selector in the aspect ratio node to cut down on size instead of manually reducing it.
- I **Highly Suggest** running several different variances of this (seed/ prompts/ etc.), then choosing the best images

en.text:
## Instructions:


## 🛑🚫✋I HIGHLY suggest that you fix the seed, run the images at **low resolution** on the custom/ test prompt, then make your adjustments before doing a full run.


**Smart Denoise**  
- Removes noise while trying to keep detail  
- Sigma: higher = smoother, lower = more detail  
- Threshold: how aggressive the denoise is  
- Radius Multiplier: higher for noisy images, lower for clean ones  
💡 Start gentle. Only raise values if the image is actually noisy.

**Color Match**  
- Matches colors to a reference image (usually Image 2)  
- Method: “adain” is the most common and stable  
- Strength: 0–1  

**Sharpen Pro**  
- Adaptive mid-tone contrast / micro-contrast  
- Radius, strength, blend mode, shadow/highlight controls  
💡 Super important node. Adds “pop” without the cardboard cut-out look.

**Image Adjust (LCImageAdjust)**  
- Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Sharpness, Blur  
- Brightness center = 0  
- Contrast & Saturation center = 1

steps.title: Load Image 📷
steps.text:
Load your character's face here and set the dataset's size.

✋ I cannot stress enough: 🗑️ in, 🗑️ out. Load a clean, high quality, front facing headshot.

settings.why: An upper torso headshot only.

steps.title: Load Image 2 🖼️
steps.text:
Optional. A second image helps strengthen the different facial expressions. Turn it on with the Use Image 2 switch.

💡 I suggest a smiling one here and a serious one up top.

steps.title: 📐 LC Aspect Ratio Simplifier
steps.text: This controls the generation size and aspect ratio of the image as well as resolution

settings.why: the higher this is, teh larger (and mor VRAM and ⏱️ it uses
use custom or a preset 💡I highly suggest running a few sets at different aspect ratios so you get a better mix

steps.title: ⚙️ User Settings
steps.text:
Name your character, set the anchors and pick the prompt list.

⚠️ The program defaults to the original image's clothing 👗👚. The prompts and the Reference Boost overcome it.

settings.why: Name your character. It goes into the file names.
The anchor text ⚓ for your character, e.g. "fit, blonde hair, green eyes, medium breasts".
Keeps clothing from transferring and adds a few quality words. Made for realism, so leave it alone.
Choose one of the prompt lists, or make your own in the Custom list.
Anywhere between 8 and 10. It really differs between models.
Fix the seed while you test, then run several variations (seed, prompts) and pick the best images.
Realism or style LoRAs go here. I have no character LoRAs, so try one and let me know.

steps.title: Prompt List Group 📝✅
steps.text:
Every line is one image in the dataset. Review the prompts to make sure they match your character.

💡 Each new line is a prompt, so be careful with line breaks.

settings.why: Custom & test. Run your low resolution tests here first, then do a full run.
The base list: front, sides, rear, close-up and outfits.

steps.title: 🎨 Post Processing
steps.text:
Denoise, color match, sharpening and adjustments for the whole dataset.

🛑 I HIGHLY suggest you fix the seed, run the images at low resolution on the custom/test prompt, then make your adjustments before doing a full run.

settings.why: Start gentle. Only raise it if the image is actually noisy.
Matches colors to a reference image. adain is the most common and stable.
Sharpen Pro: super important node. Adds "pop" without the cardboard cut-out look.
Brightness center = 0.

steps.title: 💾 Save Group
steps.text: Saves every image with a matching text file of its prompt, ready for LoRA training.

settings.why: Run #. Added to the prefix so you can tell the runs apart. It adds 1 after every run. Reset as necessary.
⚠️ Super important: switch between .txt and .json based on the LoRA trainer you use.
